verdicts.rewritten_summary: CNC3 (23 Aug 2024): the PNM Constitution Review Committee rejected adding sexual-orientation protections to the national constitution (decision announced at a special convention); CAISO's Dr Angelique Nixon said the community has 'been waiting far too long for equal rights and protection'. Documents LGBTQ-rights exclusion from the 2024 constitutional-review process.

GlobalGayz (Aug 2012): travel/culture profile stating that although homosexuality is illegal 'the laws are mostly ignored' in practice; describes tourist-facing social scene and island context. Usable as a 2012 non-enforcement baseline; predates the 2018 decriminalisation ruling, so dated for current-law purposes.

PinkNews (21 Nov 2017): first-person appeal by activist Jason Jones during his High Court challenge to T&T's same-sex criminalisation — he faces up to 25 years' imprisonment for consensual sex with an adult male partner; article carries the litigation campaign. Marks the constitutional challenge that put the criminal law in play.

Erasing 76 Crimes (23 Jun 2016): PM Keith Rowley told Parliament (17 Jun 2016) the state must protect all citizens 'regardless of whom they sleep with', while refusing to repeal the same-sex criminal laws; cites Newsday. Documents the reform-refusal gap in official rhetoric as of 2016.

Amnesty International (11 Feb 2025): at least 84 people — mainly gay men and trans women — arrested, arbitrarily detained and prosecuted in Tunis, Hammamet, Sousse and El Kef between 26 Sep 2024 and 31 Jan 2025 on 'public indecency'/morality charges; a 31 Oct 2024 mass conviction drew prison terms up to 4.5 years, upheld on appeal 5 Feb 2025 (four released after reduction). Quantified 2024-25 crackdown evidence.

Cairo 52 country page: Penal Code Article 230 criminalises same-sex conduct with up to 3 years' imprisonment; records enforcement (e.g. Oct 2021 arrest of two transgender women under morality/debauchery provisions) and gaps in legal gender recognition. Primary-law summary for visitor risk.

Intersection Association (Nov 2024): transgender women in Tunisian prisons are processed under their former names and birth gender in detention records, arrest processes and court hearings — systemic identity refusal from detention onward, described as continuous suffering and discrimination inside the prison system. Direct trans-specific custodial-risk evidence.

Cairo 52 (30 Jan 2024): reports the Tunis Court of First Instance's Apr 2023 refusal of legal gender recognition to a transgender man; the court weighed contradictory lower-court judgements (incl. case No. 12304/2018) and found no consistent precedent, leaving recognition unsettled below the Court of Cassation. Shows LGR is court-by-court and often denied.

Human Rights Watch (29 Mar 2016): documents at least seven men prosecuted for consensual same-sex conduct in two cases over six months, all convicted under Penal Code art. 230 (up to 3 years); interviewed detainees reported beatings, forced anal examinations and humiliating treatment by police. Core enforcement-abuse evidence.

Erasing 76 Crimes (27 Sep 2017): Tunisia pledged to the UN to stop forced anal testing in homosexuality cases, but kept the anti-gay law itself; Kapitalis warns the pledge does not decriminalise anything. Shows reform-by-commitment without legal change.

url.claim: Human Rights Watch (Oct 2025): 'Türkiye: Draft Law Threatens LGBT People with Prison' — a proposed penal-code package would effectively criminalise LGBT people with long prison terms.

verdicts.rewritten_summary: Human Rights Watch (29 Oct 2025): a draft legislative package would effectively criminalise LGBT people under vague claims of protecting 'the family' and 'public morals' — framing the Erdoğan government has repeatedly used to legitimise stigmatisation; sets the reform backdrop as authoritarian drift. Key legislative-risk evidence for 2025-26.

url.claim: Kaos GL (Feb 2026): 'A major siege' against LGBTI+ people in 2025 - hostility turned into state policy; the LGBTI+ Human Rights Report 2025 ('The Year of the Family: A Major Siege Against LGBTI+ People') documents institutionalised anti-LGBTI policies, hate speech from senior officials, and instructions to public institutions under the 'Year of the Family' banner creating a climate encouraging human-rights violations.

verdicts.rewritten_summary: Kaos GL (Feb 2026): the LGBTI+ Human Rights Report 2025 records 313 violations in 2025 — about two-and-a-half times 2024 — dominated by detention (299 detention decisions: 256 on record, 43 off the record), plus systematic privacy attacks; frames hostility turned into state policy. Quantified annual evidence.

url.claim: bianet (Aug 2025): Istanbul police detain ~20 trans women for ID checks amid profiling concerns - stopped on the street, while shopping or in cafés in Beyoğlu, held at Taksim Şehit Haşim Usta Police Station and released after 'General Information Gathering' (GBT) background checks; legal experts argue GBT checks violate ECHR Article 5; one detainee: 'They didn't fine us, but they documented us. The new law hasn't even passed yet, but they're already enforcing it on us.'
Turkish Minute (Feb 2026): report documents sharp rise in LGBTQ rights violations in Turkey in 2025 - coverage of the Kaos GL report findings.

verdicts.rewritten_summary: Turkish Minute (26 Feb 2026): covers the Kaos GL 2025 report — hundreds of cases documented via media monitoring and civil-society complaints; six deaths linked to anti-LGBTQ violence in 2025, three classified as hate killings; transgender individuals disproportionately affected. Second reporting of the annual data.

url.claim: Truth Justice Memory Center et al. (Aug 2025): 'You should have behaved yourself!' - 2025 Istanbul Trans and LGBTI+ Pride Week monitoring report by seven human-rights organisations documenting violations during and after the 11th Trans Pride March and 23rd Istanbul LGBTI+ Pride March; systematic violations ongoing since 2015, with senior officials using discriminatory rhetoric.

verdicts.rewritten_summary: Truth Justice Memory Center (Aug 2025): monitoring of the 2025 Istanbul Trans and LGBTI+ Pride Week — violations of international human-rights law continuing since 2015 persisted through 2025; senior officials' discriminatory rhetoric deepened homophobia and transphobia, and discrimination against LGBTI+ people and their allies was entrenched. Event-monitoring evidence.

url.claim: Kaos GL (Sept 2025): a new Health Ministry regulation may profile trans people and restrict transition access - 'gender reassignment' added to official reasons for medical board reports; e-reports replace paper; boards must now include six specialities examining applicants separately; the ministry says it 'does not grant a new right' but strengthens 'control and monitoring mechanisms'.

verdicts.rewritten_summary: Kaos GL (Sept 2025): a new Health Ministry regulation risks profiling trans people — after a Kayseri Provincial Health Directorate circular added 'gender reassignment' to official reasons for medical-board reports, hospitals were barred from the 'other' option and told to issue e-reports, with online framing contested as an 'LGBT opening'. Transition-access regulatory drift.

url.claim: Kaos GL (Aug 2024): transphobic attack in Istanbul - trans woman Yaşam was attacked with a knife by a 17-year-old in Bakırköy; the victim was detained and spent the night in a detention centre while the attacker was released; 'The detention of the victim trans woman, not the knife attacker, reveals the hate policy of the Turkish state.'

verdicts.rewritten_summary: Kaos GL (Aug 2024): trans woman Yaşam was knifed by a 17-year-old in Bakırköy; the perpetrator was released while the victim was referred for arrest — activists call the detention asymmetry evidence of a state hate policy. Concrete 2024 violence + policing-asymmetry case.

verdicts.rewritten_summary: Nomad Lawyer (2026): Turkey's passport-carrying rule for foreigners — original photo ID required at transit checkpoints in holiday destinations, with fines up to 3,000 Turkish lira for non-compliance and detention warnings. Direct visitor-facing document-risk evidence.

url.claim: Human Rights Watch (May 2008): launch of the 123-page report 'We Need a Law for Liberation' — documents a long, continuing history of violence and abuse based on sexual orientation and gender identity and calls for legal reform, urging the EU to tie membership prospects to ending the abuses.

verdicts.rewritten_summary: Human Rights Watch (22 May 2008): launches the 123-page report 'We Need a Law for Liberation' from 70+ interviews over three years — documents a continuing history of beatings, robberies and abuse against gay men and transgender people in Turkey. Foundational historical evidence; dated (pre-2018 legal changes).

url.claim: ILGA World Database jurisdiction page for Tuvalu: documents the legal status — male same-sex conduct criminalised under colonial-era provisions.

US State Department 2013 Human Rights Report for Tuvalu: traditional customs perpetuate religious and social discrimination including against women; no government abuses; the LGBT section notes criminalisation under the Penal Code but no prosecutions.

Tuvalu Ministry of Health Global AIDS Progress Report 2017 (UNAIDS): the national HIV response, drawing on the Pacific Multi-Country Mapping and Behavioural Study on HIV and STI risk vulnerability among key populations (including MSM and transgender Tuvaluans).
US Mission in Geneva (March 2011): post on LGBT rights in the UN context - Tuvalu was among Pacific countries signing the joint statement of support for decriminalisation and SOGI rights.

verdicts.rewritten_summary: US Mission Geneva (22 Mar 2011): Tuvalu appears among roughly 80 signatory states of the UN joint statement recalling General Assembly resolutions on human rights, sexual orientation and gender identity; also lists Asia-Pacific Forum and Council of Europe mechanisms used to press the issue. Documents Tuvalu's 2011 diplomatic position; dated but on-topic.

url.claim: GlobalGayz archive of Tuvalu news and reports: includes the OHCHR op-ed 'Decriminalizing Homosexuality - first step to establish equality' (Oct 2011) noting Tuvalu among Pacific countries supporting the UN call.

verdicts.rewritten_summary: GlobalGayz Tuvalu archive: aggregates news and reports incl. an OHCHR Human Rights Day op-ed urging states to decriminalise consensual same-sex relations, plus historical items on Tuvalu's colonial-era sodomy-law status. Useful as a dated context and pointer source rather than primary authority.
